world.title: Trump envoys’ plan to shift frozen Russian assets to U.S. rejected
world.summary: The United States proposed that European countries unfreeze some Russian sovereign assets and place them in a financial vehicle overseen by Washington, but European officials rejected the plan during talks in Miami on Oct. 9, the Financial Times reported. President Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner present
world.content: The United States proposed that European countries unfreeze some Russian sovereign assets and place them in a financial vehicle overseen by Washington, but European officials rejected the plan during talks in Miami on Oct. 9, the Financial Times reported. President Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner presented several possible mechanisms during discussions on a comprehensive peace agreement for Ukraine. About €260 billion in Russian central bank assets have been frozen in Western countries since Russia’s 2022 invasion, including roughly €193 billion held at Belgium-based Euroclear. Washington was considering offering the funds as an incentive for a partial ceasefire, rather than as a reward after one took effect, according to reporting cited by Meduza. European officials said they would not cede control of the assets or return any portion to Moscow. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the assets should remain frozen in Europe, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow was unaware of the reported U.S. initiative and questioned the report’s reliability.
world.image_alt: Trump envoys’ plan to shift frozen Russian assets to U.S. rejected

world.title: EU leaders split over €1.62 trillion budget as deadline nears
world.summary: European Union leaders opened two days of talks in Brussels on Oct. 15, sharply divided over the bloc’s 2028–2034 budget, as several leaders opposed an Irish compromise proposal that would set spending at €1.62 trillion. The proposal is €141 billion below the European Commission’s opening plan, but net contributors inc
world.content: European Union leaders opened two days of talks in Brussels on Oct. 15, sharply divided over the bloc’s 2028–2034 budget, as several leaders opposed an Irish compromise proposal that would set spending at €1.62 trillion. The proposal is €141 billion below the European Commission’s opening plan, but net contributors including Germany and Sweden say it remains too large; Sweden says it would raise its net contribution by almost 60%. The dispute centres on how to finance new priorities such as defence and competitiveness without cutting support for agriculture and poorer regions. Ireland says its proposal balances those demands, while France and other governments want more investment and new EU-wide revenue sources. The European Parliament has also objected to reductions in research, civil protection and infrastructure. Leaders aim to reach a political agreement by the end of 2026, but the summit is not expected to produce a breakthrough. European Council President António Costa will lead further negotiations, including a special meeting planned for late November. The European Parliament and all 27 member states must then approve the package before it can take effect on Jan. 1, 2028.
world.image_alt: EU leaders split over €1.62 trillion budget as deadline nears

world.title: Russia detains Swede who fought for Ukraine over alleged sabotage plot
world.summary: Russia’s Federal Security Service says it detained a Swedish citizen in the Pskov region, accusing him of illegally crossing the border to plan sabotage and attacks on military facilities. The FSB alleges he served as a drone-unit commander in Ukraine’s 24th Separate Assault Battalion from February to June 2026 and ent
world.content: Russia’s Federal Security Service says it detained a Swedish citizen in the Pskov region, accusing him of illegally crossing the border to plan sabotage and attacks on military facilities. The FSB alleges he served as a drone-unit commander in Ukraine’s 24th Separate Assault Battalion from February to June 2026 and entered Russia under the pretext of joining its armed forces. It has opened a case over illegal border crossing and is considering terrorism and mercenary charges. Russian state media showed footage in which the man identified himself as Freddy Mikael Stalkrantz Lindholm, 35, and described his service in Ukraine. His relatives confirmed to Swedish television that he had fought for Ukraine, but the sabotage allegations have not been independently verified. Sweden’s prime minister said the government would investigate through its embassy in Moscow. Ukraine had not commented by the time of publication. The arrest followed the FSB’s detention of a Japanese newspaper correspondent on espionage allegations earlier in the week.
world.image_alt: Russia detains Swede who fought for Ukraine over alleged sabotage plot

world.title: Two cargo ships sink near Hormuz as attacks threaten shipping
world.summary: Two cargo ships sank near the Strait of Hormuz in separate incidents: the Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride, hit on Tuesday, and the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier Cape Dao, struck weeks earlier on Sept. 23. All 21 crew members aboard GFS Pride were evacuated without injury; one crew member died in t
world.content: Two cargo ships sank near the Strait of Hormuz in separate incidents: the Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride, hit on Tuesday, and the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier Cape Dao, struck weeks earlier on Sept. 23. All 21 crew members aboard GFS Pride were evacuated without injury; one crew member died in the attack on Cape Dao, while the rest escaped. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said GFS Pride hit a naval mine while using an unauthorized route, but maritime authorities described projectile strikes. The cause has not been independently established. Attacks on commercial vessels have increased sharply. Iran has said it is intensifying strikes in response to the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports and new sanctions, while two senior Iranian officials told Reuters the change in tactics is also intended to keep oil prices high and influence the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections. Before the war began on Feb. 28, the strait carried about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade. Shipping data cited by CNN showed that just 4.147 million barrels of oil passed through on Monday, less than a quarter of prewar levels.
world.image_alt: Two cargo ships sink near Hormuz as attacks threaten shipping

world.title: Albanian students escalate protests as Rama rejects resignation calls
world.summary: Student-led protests in Albania entered a third day on Thursday, with thousands demonstrating in Tirana as riot police used tear gas and water cannon during clashes. Protesters demand Prime Minister Edi Rama’s resignation, citing university conditions, rising education costs, limited job prospects and corruption. The u
world.content: Student-led protests in Albania entered a third day on Thursday, with thousands demonstrating in Tirana as riot police used tear gas and water cannon during clashes. Protesters demand Prime Minister Edi Rama’s resignation, citing university conditions, rising education costs, limited job prospects and corruption. The unrest has also spread beyond the capital. Authorities reported injuries among police and civilians, as well as arrests, after demonstrators attacked or damaged government buildings, banks and businesses. Parliament postponed a session scheduled for Thursday as violence continued. Rama rejected calls to quit, saying governments change through elections and that he is prepared to discuss education costs. He said Albanians had given him a mandate to complete EU membership negotiations and condemned attacks on institutions and public property. The demonstrations follow months of largely peaceful protests against a proposed luxury resort on Albania’s southern coast linked to U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner. The project has faced legal challenges, and Reuters reported that it found no evidence of wrongdoing by Kushner. Albania aims to join the EU as early as 2028.
world.image_alt: Albanian students escalate protests as Rama rejects resignation calls

world.title: Saudi-led coalition says Houthi attacks killed 17 at Riyadh airport as Saudi-Iran tensions rise
world.summary: The Saudi-led military coalition said Thursday that Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed 17 people and wounded 333 between Oct. 7 and 11. It said the Houthis attempted 20 attacks on the airport this month. The coalition also said it had destroyed 127 Houthi weapons depots and launch plat
world.content: The Saudi-led military coalition said Thursday that Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed 17 people and wounded 333 between Oct. 7 and 11. It said the Houthis attempted 20 attacks on the airport this month. The coalition also said it had destroyed 127 Houthi weapons depots and launch platforms in Yemen. On Wednesday, a Houthi strike hit an administrative building at Saudi oil company Aramco’s headquarters in Dhahran, causing a limited fire. Saudi officials reported no casualties there. The Houthis have threatened further attacks and warned airlines that Saudi airspace and airports are unsafe. Saudi officials accused Iran of encouraging the escalation and supplying weapons and training. The Houthis have previously denied being an Iranian proxy, and Tehran has rejected that description. Fighting has also intensified in Yemen, where Saudi-backed forces are trying to retake Houthi-held positions near the Red Sea coast and Bab al-Mandeb. The attacks have disrupted Saudi-hosted events: the EU-Gulf Cooperation Council summit planned for next week was postponed, and organizers of Riyadh’s Future Investment Initiative offered remote participation after oil executives withdrew. Saudi officials say they remain in direct contact with Iran and had asked the Houthis to meet in Oman, but the group refused, according to Deputy Foreign Minister Rayed Krimly.
world.image_alt: Saudi-led coalition says Houthi attacks killed 17 at Riyadh airport as Saudi-Iran tensions rise

world.title: Pope Leo resumes work and Mass as lung recovery progresses
world.summary: Pope Leo XIV resumed work at Rome’s Gemelli hospital Thursday, met Vatican chief of staff Archbishop Paolo Rudelli and celebrated Mass with priests for a second day. Doctors said his recovery from lung-cancer surgery was progressing as expected. His latest chest X-ray showed the operated lung was recovering well, routi
world.content: Pope Leo XIV resumed work at Rome’s Gemelli hospital Thursday, met Vatican chief of staff Archbishop Paolo Rudelli and celebrated Mass with priests for a second day. Doctors said his recovery from lung-cancer surgery was progressing as expected. His latest chest X-ray showed the operated lung was recovering well, routine test results remained within normal ranges and he was performing daily activities independently, the medical team said. Doctors are awaiting results that could establish the cancer’s molecular characteristics and whether it has spread beyond the removed lung tissue. Those findings will guide decisions on further treatment. The Vatican has canceled public engagements through Oct. 20. Leo’s Nov. 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru remains on the Vatican’s schedule, but Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori said recovery could take several weeks and the visit may need to change. The 12-day itinerary includes more than 31,000 kilometers of travel and a visit to Cusco, about 3,400 meters above sea level.
world.image_alt: Pope Leo resumes work and Mass as lung recovery progresses

world.title: Tanker fire off Romania leaves seven missing as Black Sea ship attacks mount
world.summary: Romanian rescuers searched Thursday for seven missing crew members after the San Marino-flagged chemical tanker Wine Trader caught fire near Sulina in the Black Sea; five of its 12 crew members were rescued. The tanker sent a distress call at about 7 a.m. after reporting explosions. A second vessel, the Comoros-flagged
world.content: Romanian rescuers searched Thursday for seven missing crew members after the San Marino-flagged chemical tanker Wine Trader caught fire near Sulina in the Black Sea; five of its 12 crew members were rescued. The tanker sent a distress call at about 7 a.m. after reporting explosions. A second vessel, the Comoros-flagged chemical and oil tanker Yara J, caught fire late Wednesday near the Sulina Canal, but all 17 crew members were safe. Romanian President Nicușor Dan said both ships had been hit by drones but declined to say whether the drones were Russian. Romania’s defense minister said an investigation was underway, and officials had not established responsibility. Romanian authorities reported drone activity in the area and an overnight airspace incursion. Other commercial vessels have been attacked near Romania and Bulgaria, both NATO members. The two countries’ leaders were due to meet NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte in Brussels on Thursday; Bulgaria’s prime minister said EU leaders would discuss a proposed moratorium on attacks against civilian ships.
world.image_alt: Tanker fire off Romania leaves seven missing as Black Sea ship attacks mount

business.title: Houthis threaten more Saudi oil strikes after Aramco headquarters attack
business.summary: Yemen’s Houthi movement vowed Wednesday to continue attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities after a strike hit Saudi Aramco’s headquarters in Dhahran the previous evening. Saudi Arabia’s energy ministry reported a limited fire and no injuries, while people familiar with the incident told Reuters that the building
business.content: Yemen’s Houthi movement vowed Wednesday to continue attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities after a strike hit Saudi Aramco’s headquarters in Dhahran the previous evening. Saudi Arabia’s energy ministry reported a limited fire and no injuries, while people familiar with the incident told Reuters that the building sustained extensive damage. Aramco operations continued. Brent crude traded above $106 a barrel on Wednesday, and Aramco shares fell 0.5% in early trading. The International Monetary Fund’s managing director warned that the attacks could have negative spillovers worldwide. The IMF forecast that Saudi Arabia’s economy would contract 3.3% in 2026 before growing 7.9% in 2027. It prepared those estimates before the deadly airport attack. Its recovery outlook assumes the Strait of Hormuz will begin reopening gradually in March 2027 and shipping will return to pre-war conditions by October. Riyadh’s international airport is closed until October 17, and airlines have canceled flights to Saudi Arabia.
business.image_alt: Houthis threaten more Saudi oil strikes after Aramco headquarters attack

business.title: Brazilian Senate approves 40-hour workweek before presidential runoff
business.summary: Brazil’s Senate approved a constitutional amendment on Wednesday, Oct. 14, to reduce the maximum workweek from 44 to 40 hours without cutting pay and end the six-day “6x1” schedule. Senators voted 75-1 for the reform, which provides for two weekly rest days; the government estimates more than 37 million workers could b
business.content: Brazil’s Senate approved a constitutional amendment on Wednesday, Oct. 14, to reduce the maximum workweek from 44 to 40 hours without cutting pay and end the six-day “6x1” schedule. Senators voted 75-1 for the reform, which provides for two weekly rest days; the government estimates more than 37 million workers could benefit. Six-day schedules will end and the workweek limit will drop to 42 hours 60 days after the amendment is formally promulgated; the limit will fall to 40 hours after a further 14 months. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva backed the change ahead of the Oct. 25 runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro, who reversed his opposition shortly before the vote. Brazil’s National Confederation of Industry forecast higher payroll costs and price increases.
business.image_alt: Brazilian Senate approves 40-hour workweek before presidential runoff

business.title: Bank of America fine cuts quarterly earnings by 17 cents per share
business.summary: Bank of America said it will record the $1.2 billion penalty announced by U.S. regulators as a non-tax-deductible charge in its third-quarter results, reducing quarterly earnings by about 17 cents per share. The bank’s shares fell 2.7% in after-hours trading after closing down 1.1%. The penalty followed regulators’ fin
business.content: Bank of America said it will record the $1.2 billion penalty announced by U.S. regulators as a non-tax-deductible charge in its third-quarter results, reducing quarterly earnings by about 17 cents per share. The bank’s shares fell 2.7% in after-hours trading after closing down 1.1%. The penalty followed regulators’ findings that the bank’s monitoring system delayed suspicious-activity reports on billions of dollars in transactions. The bank must also hire an independent firm to review past transactions. UBS analyst Erika Najarian said the charge could add to investor concerns about expenses and the bank’s roughly $6 billion quarterly share-buyback pace. She also noted that regulators did not impose an asset cap.
business.image_alt: Bank of America fine cuts quarterly earnings by 17 cents per share

business.title: KPMG survey: AI agents boost efficiency, but few CEOs see transformation
business.summary: A KPMG survey of 400 CEOs at large U.S. companies found that AI agents are producing efficiency or growth gains for many businesses, but only 9% of leaders described the technology as transformational today. About four in 10 reported significant improvements, while a similar share saw moderate effects in specific uses.
business.content: A KPMG survey of 400 CEOs at large U.S. companies found that AI agents are producing efficiency or growth gains for many businesses, but only 9% of leaders described the technology as transformational today. About four in 10 reported significant improvements, while a similar share saw moderate effects in specific uses. KPMG US chief executive Tim Walsh said companies must overhaul processes and prepare their data to get more from AI, rather than simply install tools. While 53% of CEOs plan workforce reductions in some areas, 89% expect to add employees over the next three years, mostly in small increments. CEOs also expect to redesign roles and train or hire workers for human-AI collaboration. More than eight in 10 ranked AI among their top investment priorities for the next three years, and roughly two-thirds plan to devote at least 10% of next year’s capital budgets to it.
business.image_alt: KPMG survey: AI agents boost efficiency, but few CEOs see transformation

business.title: Anthropic reports $16.8 billion in quarterly revenue ahead of planned November IPO
business.summary: Anthropic told prospective investors its revenue reached $16.8 billion in the third quarter, up about 45% from the previous quarter, as the AI company prepares to go public. The company also reported a second consecutive quarter of adjusted profit, positive free cash flow and an 11% operating margin, though it has not
business.content: Anthropic told prospective investors its revenue reached $16.8 billion in the third quarter, up about 45% from the previous quarter, as the AI company prepares to go public. The company also reported a second consecutive quarter of adjusted profit, positive free cash flow and an 11% operating margin, though it has not published a full prospectus or specified which costs its adjusted measure excludes. Anthropic is targeting an IPO in November, potentially at a valuation of up to $2 trillion. Formal marketing could begin the week of Nov. 9, with trading planned before Thanksgiving on Nov. 26, but those dates remain subject to change. Revenue growth slowed from the previous quarter, and annualized revenue is expected to finish 2026 below $100 billion, short of some backers’ earlier expectations.
business.image_alt: Anthropic reports $16.8 billion in quarterly revenue ahead of planned November IPO

business.title: US producer prices jump 6.3% as energy costs surge
business.summary: U.S. producer prices rose 1.3% in September from August and 6.3% from a year earlier. The monthly increase was the largest since March 2022, and the annual rate was the highest since December 2022. The increase exceeded economists’ forecasts. Final-demand energy prices climbed 10.8%, accounting for more than 80% of the
business.content: U.S. producer prices rose 1.3% in September from August and 6.3% from a year earlier. The monthly increase was the largest since March 2022, and the annual rate was the highest since December 2022. The increase exceeded economists’ forecasts. Final-demand energy prices climbed 10.8%, accounting for more than 80% of the rise in goods prices, while gasoline prices rose 20.3%. Services prices also increased. Reports linked higher energy costs to the U.S.-Iran conflict and constraints on oil supply. A separate report showed retail sales growth slowed to 0.8% in September from 1.3% in August, with sales excluding gas stations up just 0.2%. Some producer-price data feed into the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge, the personal consumption expenditures price index. The Fed’s next meeting is scheduled for Oct. 27-28.
business.image_alt: US producer prices jump 6.3% as energy costs surge

business.title: UK economy grows 0.1% in August as factories offset weak services
business.summary: Britain’s gross domestic product rose 0.1% in August, beating economists’ forecast of a 0.1% contraction but slowing from 0.4% growth in July. Production expanded 0.8%, its fastest monthly rise in nine months, with manufacturing up 1.2%; services were flat and construction fell 0.2%. GDP grew 0.7% over the three months
business.content: Britain’s gross domestic product rose 0.1% in August, beating economists’ forecast of a 0.1% contraction but slowing from 0.4% growth in July. Production expanded 0.8%, its fastest monthly rise in nine months, with manufacturing up 1.2%; services were flat and construction fell 0.2%. GDP grew 0.7% over the three months to August. Chancellor John Healey will present the government’s Budget on 28 October. He has promised fiscal discipline and said spending plans must fit within available budgets, while pledging to address cost-of-living and business pressures. Economists have warned that higher energy costs and inflation could weigh on activity. The IMF raised its 2026 UK growth forecast to 1.3% from 1.0% earlier this week.
business.image_alt: UK economy grows 0.1% in August as factories offset weak services

business.title: Social Security announces 3.6% benefit increase for 2027
business.summary: The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment for 2027, adding about $75 a month to the average retirement benefit. The increase applies to nearly 72 million Social Security beneficiaries, with adjusted retirement payments starting in January. About 7.3 million Supplemental Security Inco
business.content: The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment for 2027, adding about $75 a month to the average retirement benefit. The increase applies to nearly 72 million Social Security beneficiaries, with adjusted retirement payments starting in January. About 7.3 million Supplemental Security Income recipients will receive the adjustment beginning Dec. 31, 2026. The announcement followed September consumer-price data showing inflation of 3.7% from a year earlier. The adjustment is calculated using consumer prices for urban wage earners and clerical workers from July through September, rather than a measure designed specifically for retirees’ spending. Senior advocates and financial experts say the formula may not reflect older people’s higher health-care costs, and Medicare Part B premiums could absorb part of the increase. The June 2026 trustees’ report projected that Social Security’s combined trust funds will be unable to pay full scheduled benefits beginning in 2034, after which incoming revenue would cover about 83% of those benefits. Congress has not enacted a permanent fix for the funding shortfall.
business.image_alt: Social Security announces 3.6% benefit increase for 2027

science.title: Voyager’s Griffin-1 lunar lander clears testing before late-2026 launch
science.summary: Voyager Technologies’ Griffin-1 lunar lander has completed acceptance testing and returned to Pittsburgh for final assembly, with launch targeted for late 2026. WPXI reported that the Pittsburgh lander passed testing, with launch planned for later this year. Final assembly follows the testing, but neither report specif
science.content: Voyager Technologies’ Griffin-1 lunar lander has completed acceptance testing and returned to Pittsburgh for final assembly, with launch targeted for late 2026. WPXI reported that the Pittsburgh lander passed testing, with launch planned for later this year. Final assembly follows the testing, but neither report specifies a launch date.
science.image_alt: Voyager’s Griffin-1 lunar lander clears testing before late-2026 launch

science.title: Study finds climate change strengthened Hurricane Polo more than El Niño
science.summary: A rapid attribution study found that human-caused climate change strengthened Hurricane Polo more than El Niño did, adding nearly 10 kph to the storm’s intensity compared with about 8 kph from El Niño. Researchers estimated that climate change made the warm conditions that fueled Polo 23 times more likely, while El Niñ
science.content: A rapid attribution study found that human-caused climate change strengthened Hurricane Polo more than El Niño did, adding nearly 10 kph to the storm’s intensity compared with about 8 kph from El Niño. Researchers estimated that climate change made the warm conditions that fueled Polo 23 times more likely, while El Niño made them 14 times more likely. The study linked Polo to waters at 31.2°C, as much as 2°C above normal. Polo intensified from a tropical storm to a Category 5 hurricane in about 24 hours and set a Pacific record by remaining at Category 5 for two and a half days. It weakened before reaching a sparsely populated part of Mexico. The study has not been peer-reviewed, and outside scientists said its estimate of climate change’s contribution may be conservative.
science.image_alt: Study finds climate change strengthened Hurricane Polo more than El Niño

science.title: Perseverance Mars sample may hold biosignature, but return plan stalls
science.summary: NASA’s Perseverance rover has collected a rock sample named Sapphire Canyon that may contain signs of ancient microbial life. The sample remains stored on Mars. It came from the Neretva river valley in Jezero Crater, and its patterned mineral spots could have formed through biological or nonbiological chemistry. Scient
science.content: NASA’s Perseverance rover has collected a rock sample named Sapphire Canyon that may contain signs of ancient microbial life. The sample remains stored on Mars. It came from the Neretva river valley in Jezero Crater, and its patterned mineral spots could have formed through biological or nonbiological chemistry. Scientists say the rover’s instruments cannot conclusively determine how the spots formed, so the sample needs laboratory study on Earth. NASA and the European Space Agency’s original sample-return plan was judged too costly and complex, and NASA has not presented a full replacement. China plans to launch its Tianwen-3 mission in 2028 and aims to return Martian samples in 2031; a private proposal would bring back 30 Perseverance samples by 2037 for less than $3 billion.
science.image_alt: Perseverance Mars sample may hold biosignature, but return plan stalls

science.title: Brazil probes Amazon fires after 1,679 blazes recorded in two weeks
science.summary: Brazilian authorities are investigating whether some recent Amazon fires were deliberately set, after 1,679 blazes were recorded in Amazonas state in the first two weeks of October—253% more than in the same period last year. Fire activity across the biome, which had been near historic lows this year, nearly tripled af
science.content: Brazilian authorities are investigating whether some recent Amazon fires were deliberately set, after 1,679 blazes were recorded in Amazonas state in the first two weeks of October—253% more than in the same period last year. Fire activity across the biome, which had been near historic lows this year, nearly tripled after Brazil’s Oct. 4 first-round election, ahead of the Oct. 25 presidential runoff. Officials have not identified who may have started the fires or established a political motive. Researchers say human activities such as land clearing and pasture renewal are the main sources of ignition, while climate change and El Niño can intensify heat and drought, allowing fires to spread. Smoke has affected Manaus, where public schools closed and residents were urged to wear masks. Federal authorities sent aircraft and firefighting teams to Amazonas, and the state declared emergencies in 36 municipalities.
science.image_alt: Brazil probes Amazon fires after 1,679 blazes recorded in two weeks

science.title: NASA tests solid-state batteries for lunar missions in extreme temperatures
science.summary: NASA has tested prototype solid-state batteries for future lunar missions, finding they could operate at temperatures as low as minus 80 degrees Celsius and survive exposure to minus 170 C without damage. The SPEARS project targets the Moon’s south pole, where nighttime temperatures can reach minus 200 C. Conventional
science.content: NASA has tested prototype solid-state batteries for future lunar missions, finding they could operate at temperatures as low as minus 80 degrees Celsius and survive exposure to minus 170 C without damage. The SPEARS project targets the Moon’s south pole, where nighttime temperatures can reach minus 200 C. Conventional lithium-ion cells rely on liquid electrolytes that can freeze in the cold and fail in high heat. The prototypes use solid ceramic- or polymer-based electrolytes. In thermal-vacuum tests, small cells operated at temperatures from minus 60 C to 80 C, with reduced performance at minus 80 C. They remained undamaged after exposure to temperatures between minus 170 C and 100 C. They cannot generate power in the most extreme cold, but NASA says small heaters could warm them when needed. The agency is developing flight test hardware, while the project’s initial phase focuses on technology development.
science.image_alt: NASA tests solid-state batteries for lunar missions in extreme temperatures

science.title: Stanford researchers revive bleached corals through contact with healthy clones
science.summary: Stanford researchers found that bleached coral fragments could recover after brief direct contact with healthy fragments from the same colony. All five treated corals in one experiment recovered within seven weeks. The treatment transfers beneficial algae and nutrients. The researchers said a few days of contact can st
science.content: Stanford researchers found that bleached coral fragments could recover after brief direct contact with healthy fragments from the same colony. All five treated corals in one experiment recovered within seven weeks. The treatment transfers beneficial algae and nutrients. The researchers said a few days of contact can start recovery, which continues after the corals are separated. Microscopy showed that the coral tissues fused, forming channels through which algae and nutrients passed. The method worked only between genetically matched corals, limiting its use on whole reefs. The team is considering culturing the algae and introducing it to bleached corals without requiring contact between genetic clones. Lead author Danny Collins said the method helps corals recover after bleaching but cannot stop the heatwaves that cause it.
science.image_alt: Stanford researchers revive bleached corals through contact with healthy clones

science.title: SpaceX cargo Dragon docks at ISS after launch lights dawn sky
science.summary: SpaceX’s CRS-35 cargo Dragon reached the International Space Station on Oct. 15, two days after a Falcon 9 launch produced a bright, jellyfish-shaped plume visible across parts of the eastern United States. The mission is SpaceX’s 35th commercial resupply flight for NASA. Dragon docked with the station’s Harmony module
science.content: SpaceX’s CRS-35 cargo Dragon reached the International Space Station on Oct. 15, two days after a Falcon 9 launch produced a bright, jellyfish-shaped plume visible across parts of the eastern United States. The mission is SpaceX’s 35th commercial resupply flight for NASA. Dragon docked with the station’s Harmony module at 9:27 a.m. EDT, delivering more than 6,300 pounds of food, research equipment and other supplies. The spacecraft also carried replacement hardware for Canadarm2 and the station toilet, along with the last of eight upgraded solar panels intended to increase the station’s power supply. The glowing plume formed when sunlight illuminated rocket exhaust high above the still-dark ground near dawn.
science.image_alt: SpaceX cargo Dragon docks at ISS after launch lights dawn sky

science.title: Study finds water triggers reactive chemistry on microplastics
science.summary: Researchers from Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley, found that micro- and nanoplastics can react with surrounding water to produce highly reactive molecules, identifying a possible mechanism for biological harm. The study, published in Nature on Oct. 14, challenges the assumption that plast
science.content: Researchers from Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley, found that micro- and nanoplastics can react with surrounding water to produce highly reactive molecules, identifying a possible mechanism for biological harm. The study, published in Nature on Oct. 14, challenges the assumption that plastic fragments remain chemically inert after breaking down. Because blood and cells contain substantial amounts of water, the team says particles reaching those environments could remain chemically active. Experiments and computer simulations suggest that water at the plastic surface helps generate radicals capable of damaging biological molecules. Laboratory tests also found changes in proteins and red blood cells, but the work does not establish the extent of any health effects in people. Researchers say the findings could guide efforts to design less reactive plastics. A Columbia team is also studying how particles move through human tissues and enter fetal and offspring tissues in animal models.
science.image_alt: Study finds water triggers reactive chemistry on microplastics

sports.title: Four arrested in shooting that wounded 49ers defensive end Keion White
sports.summary: San Francisco police arrested four men in California and Georgia in connection with the February shooting that wounded 49ers defensive end Keion White at a private Super Bowl party. Prosecutors have charged two of the men: Gregory Walker faces felony assault and firearm counts, while Curtis Green faces misdemeanor gun
sports.content: San Francisco police arrested four men in California and Georgia in connection with the February shooting that wounded 49ers defensive end Keion White at a private Super Bowl party. Prosecutors have charged two of the men: Gregory Walker faces felony assault and firearm counts, while Curtis Green faces misdemeanor gun charges. Authorities are arranging to bring the other two suspects, Marquis Davis and Antoine Washington, to San Francisco to face charges. White was shot in the ankle at the Dahlia Club shortly after 4 a.m. on Feb. 9. He recovered and has played in all five of the 49ers’ games this season. Police say their months-long investigation involved multiple agencies. Prosecutors say they will seek to hold Walker without bail pending trial. Walker and Green are due back in court on Oct. 19. The investigation remains open.
sports.image_alt: Four arrested in shooting that wounded 49ers defensive end Keion White

sports.title: DP World Tour bars 2027 LIV players as relaunch decision nears
sports.summary: The DP World Tour says golfers who plan to compete for LIV Golf in 2027 cannot join its European circuit. sports.content: The DP World Tour says golfers who plan to compete for LIV Golf in 2027 cannot join its European circuit. LIV’s lawyer called the policy an attempt to interfere with the league’s restructuring, while Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings said players must choose whether to follow its rules. LIV, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September after Saudi Arabia withdrew funding, expects to decide by the end of October whether to proceed with “LIV 2.0” or wind down. The court-supervised process includes restructuring its finances and securing enough players; the league’s lawyer said it needs a sufficient number signed by Oct. 25. Players whose LIV contracts have been rejected are no longer obligated to stay and can discuss their futures with other tours.

sports.content: Australia opened their Rugby League World Cup title defence with a 24-22 win over New Zealand in Sydney as debutant Jack Bostock scored three tries, including the 76th-minute winner. The Kangaroos trailed 22-16 before Reece Walsh’s long-range try cut the gap to two. Bostock then beat Jamayne Isaako to a high kick to put Australia ahead, and the hosts held on. New Zealand controlled much of the contest, but Australia’s defence and two first-half intercept tries helped them reach halftime level at 10-10. Kalyn Ponga scored twice for the Kiwis before leaving late with a suspected broken arm; Australia also lost halfback Mitchell Moses to a calf injury. The tournament runs through November 15, with both teams due back in action the following Sunday.

sports.content: West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth T20I in Hyderabad on October 14 to level the five-match series at 2-2. Shai Hope made an unbeaten 102 from 50 balls as West Indies scored 247-3; Keemo Paul then took five wickets as India were bowled out for 223 in 19.3 overs. Sanju Samson’s rapid 56 gave India a brisk start, but regular wickets kept the chase behind the required rate. Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy added 70 before West Indies took the remaining wickets. The fifth and final T20I is scheduled for Saturday, October 17, at Bengaluru’s M. Chinnaswamy Stadium.

sports.title: NFL cuts Rams tackle Alaric Jackson
sports.summary: The NFL reduced Los Angeles Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson’s suspension from two games to one after hearing officer Derrick Brooks reviewed his appeal. Brooks was jointly appointed by the league and the NFL Players Association. Jackson will miss Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals and can return for the Rams’
sports.content: The NFL reduced Los Angeles Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson’s suspension from two games to one after hearing officer Derrick Brooks reviewed his appeal. Brooks was jointly appointed by the league and the NFL Players Association. Jackson will miss Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals and can return for the Rams’ Oct. 25 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders. Buffalo Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb said Wednesday that his taunts before the postgame punch were about the Rams’ blocking help, not Jackson’s mother, as some had speculated. Chubb said he told Jackson that a tight end and guard would not protect him when the teams meet again. Jackson is eligible to rejoin the active roster on Oct. 19 under the reduced suspension.

sports.title: Real Madrid forward Vinícius banned for four games, to miss Barcelona Clásico
sports.summary: Real Madrid forward Vinícius Júnior received a four-match La Liga suspension for pulling Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba by the hair and protesting his red card, ruling him out of the October 25 Clásico against Barcelona. sports.content: Real Madrid forward Vinícius Júnior received a four-match La Liga suspension for pulling Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba by the hair and protesting his red card, ruling him out of the October 25 Clásico against Barcelona. The incident happened during Madrid’s 1-0 win over Villarreal: Vinícius’s apparent goal was disallowed after a VAR review, and the referee sent him off. The ban covers league matches against Sevilla on October 18, Barcelona on October 25, Racing Santander on November 1 and Valencia on November 7. Vinícius remains eligible for Champions League games. Madrid beat Roma 4-3 in that competition on Wednesday. The Spanish football federation announced the ruling about two hours before the Roma match, drawing criticism from coach José Mourinho and Vinícius. Mourinho objected to the timing; Vinícius said he learned of the suspension when he arrived at the stadium. His league return is scheduled for November 22 against Celta Vigo.

sports.title: Aston Villa beat Fenerbahce 6-0 for record European win
sports.summary: Aston Villa beat Fenerbahce 6-0 at Villa Park on October 14 for the biggest victory in the club’s European history and their first home win of the season. sports.content: Aston Villa beat Fenerbahce 6-0 at Villa Park on October 14 for the biggest victory in the club’s European history and their first home win of the season. Johan Manzambi scored on his Champions League debut, Nicolas Jackson and Ross Barkley each scored twice, and substitute Tammy Abraham completed the scoring. The result lifted Villa to six points from their first two league-phase matches, but Unai Emery said the team still needed time to settle after a summer that brought 10 new players. Villa had gone winless in their first three Premier League home games. The crowd also booed Fenerbahce forward Mason Greenwood throughout his first match in England since January 2022; charges against him were discontinued in February 2023, and he denied them. Villa’s next league match is away to Newcastle on Saturday, before they host Viking in the Champions League on October 21.

sports.title: Martínez clarifies Manchester United outburst as club weighs disciplinary action
sports.summary: Lisandro Martínez said anger and frustration drove his public criticism of Manchester United’s recruitment, but he did not withdraw his demand for greater ambition or apologize. sports.content: Lisandro Martínez said anger and frustration drove his public criticism of Manchester United’s recruitment, but he did not withdraw his demand for greater ambition or apologize. In an Instagram statement, the defender said players must take responsibility for results and reaffirmed his support for manager Michael Carrick, teammates and club staff. United are considering whether to discipline Martínez, while reports say the club’s leadership continues to back director of football Jason Wilcox. Martínez’s longer-term future at Old Trafford is also uncertain: his contract expires at the end of the season, with United holding an option to extend it by a year. Former United captain Roy Keane and ex-defender Gary Neville have since criticized Martínez’s decision to speak publicly, while differing on what it says about the club and dressing room. Carrick is due to address the dispute at his Friday media briefing before United visit Leeds on Sunday.
